we open-source TransRubric, an automatic evaluation suite for translation, which outperforms other evaluation schemes on the WMT26 metrics shared task test set and is more stable with respect to human evaluation.
Tencent Hunyuan Team
Mao Zheng, Zheng Li, Fangxu Liu, Tao Chen, Bingxin Qu, Bo Lv, Mingrui Sun
As strong models converge on standard benchmarks, holistic scores and neural metrics (Guerreiro et al., 2023; Rei et al., 2022) struggle to distinguish them or to explain where they fail.
We need an evaluation method that is fine-grained, interpretable and consistent with human judgments, both to measure progress and to guide model development.
To evaluate translation quality in a fine-grained and interpretable way, we develop TransRubric
LLM-as-a-judge (Zheng et al., 2023; Kocmi & Federmann, 2023) evaluation suite, and use it as the primary metric throughout this report.

a TransRubric judge checks the candidate against a translation rubric, identifies each issue together with its error type (e.g., completeness, accuracy, terminology and instruction following) and severity level
outputs a pointwise score on a 0–100 scale

TransRubric supports both reference-based evaluation (used for FLORES-200, WMT26, Mandarin⇔Minority and HardMTBench) and reference-free evaluation (used for WildMTBench-202611, which has no reference translations).
each TransRubric score is the arithmetic mean of two judges, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash … and Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (Qwen Team, 2026a).
To make scores comparable across models, each benchmark score is computed with the fixed expected number of samples as the denominator, so empty outputs and unscored samples count as 0.
We validate TransRubric on Task 2 (segment-level quality score prediction) of the WMT26 shared task on automated translation quality evaluation (Lavie et al., 2026)
screen-based Pairwise Difference Pearson (PDP) at the segment level, source-based Soft Pairwise Accuracy (SPA) at the system level, and their average (Avg Corr)
In this experiment, TransRubric runs reference-free with Gemini 3.6 Flash as the underlying judge.
TransRubric achieves the highest PDP (0.744) and Avg Corr (0.832), ahead of the top-ranked official submission Gemini-3.6-Flash (0.736 / 0.830)
Its system-level SPA (0.920) is on par with the best system (0.924), and all LLM-based evaluators clearly outperform conventional metrics such as chrF, COMET22 and xCOMET.
We further compare TransRubric with 10 professional annotators majoring in English on 651 translations
217 source texts with three candidate translations each, covering both Chinese→English and English→Chinese
Each annotator scores every translation once on a 0–100 scale, and TransRubric (with the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Qwen3.5-397B-A17B judges) scores every translation 10 times.
Across the 10 human annotators, the per-sample standard deviation averages 15.57 points, whereas across the 10 TransRubric runs it averages only 3.31 points (average variance 285.79 vs. 26.20).
For the three translations of each source text, we form all pairs (651 pairs in total) and check whether each rater prefers the same translation as the gold standard.
Since the gold standard is built on the annotators’ own scores, this comparison may favor the human annotators.

TransRubric reaches 59.91%, ranking 4th among the 11 raters: it is higher than 7 of the 10 annotators and lower only than three of them (61.29%, 60.37% and 60.06%), well above the human average of 54.7%.
TransRubric is released together with Hy-MT3 at https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy-MT3.

TransRubric is a rubric-based LLM-as-a-judge evaluation method for fine-grained and interpretable translation quality assessment.

Given a translation task, a candidate translation, and a task-specific rubric, a TransRubric judge identifies concrete issues with their error categories and severity levels, and produces a pointwise translation quality score on a 0–100 scale.

This repository releases resources for applying TransRubric: sample-specific rubrics for four test sets derived from FLORES-200, WMT26 GenMT, and HardMTBench, prompt templates for constructing translation rubrics, and the pointwise translation judge prompt.
The source texts, references, instructions, and benchmark-specific metadata come from the corresponding upstream benchmarks; the sample-specific `rubric` field is the added evaluation resource.

`RUBRIC_DRAFT_PROMPT` generates an initial source-grounded rubric.
`RUBRIC_DELTA_PROMPT` identifies missing discriminative criteria from unlabeled candidate translations.
`RUBRIC_MERGE_PROMPT` conservatively merges valid new criteria into the rubric.
Rubric items are written in Simplified Chinese and are intended to be concrete, verifiable checks rather than rigid reference translations.
It returns structured issues, an overall summary, a confidence value, and a translation quality score from 0 to 100.
The rubric is a verification checklist, not a reference answer or evidence that an error exists.
Equivalent and natural translations should be accepted.

TransRubric is a rubric-based LLM-as-a-judge evaluation suite for fine-grained and interpretable translation quality assessment.
a TransRubric judge checks the candidate against a sample-specific rubric, identifies each issue together with its error type and severity, and outputs a pointwise score on a 0–100 scale.

On Task 2 of the WMT26 shared task on automated translation quality evaluation, TransRubric achieves the highest segment-level PDP (0.744) and Avg Corr (0.832), ahead of the top-ranked official submission.

Compared with 10 professional annotators on 651 Chinese⇔English translations, the per-sample standard deviation of TransRubric scores across 10 runs is only 3.31 points, versus 15.57 points across human annotators.
Its pairwise accuracy (59.91%) is higher than 7 of the 10 annotators.

We release sample-specific rubrics for FLORES-200 (33 languages and 64 lower-resource languages), WMT26 GenMT and HardMTBench, together with the rubric construction prompts and the translation judge prompt.
